In Al-Adsani v. the United Kingdom (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001), the Court held that immunities were not in conflict with the right to a fair trial. Upholding Kuwait’s state immunity was treated as a proportionate limit on access to court under a generally recognised rule of international law, so the United Kingdom had not violated Article 6 § 1 (nine votes to eight) or Article 3. The jus cogens status of the torture prohibition did not displace that immunity in a civil damages claim.

CONFIDENCE: 76
